label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday at Embakasi: casuals' pay, notes for Brian

Brian,

This is for you to read on Sunday. Everything here is checked against Kevin's and NW's emails and what Peninah and Joseph sent me today. It's long-ish but I've tried to keep it to what you'll actually need standing in front of them.

1. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED ON FRIDAY

Nobody was paid. Not partly, not some people. Zero.

Finance sent the casuals' bulk payment file to the bank as usual: 212 people, KES 1,846,300 in total. The bank had upgraded its system on 25 November and changed the file template. Our file still had the old layout. One column (the beneficiary reference) was longer than the new 20-character limit, so the bank rejected the whole file at 1:52pm Friday. Nothing in it was processed.

The rejection alert went to an old finance mailbox, so Kevin only saw it after 5. By then the bank's cut-off had passed.

That's the whole story. A file format change at the bank, and a notification that went to the wrong inbox. You can tell the guys exactly that.

2. WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

We're not waiting for the bank again. NW approved paying the whole lot through M-Pesa bulk instead. Kevin's realistic time is money on phones Monday by 11am. He has been clear he won't promise earlier, and neither should you.

The same M-Pesa batch will also carry:
- KES 500 per head for Monday lunch and fare, for every casual on the affected list. This is on top of their pay.
- All M-Pesa charges are on the company. Nobody gets anything deducted for the transfer.

Worth knowing: a lot of them have rent due on the 1st, which is Tuesday. Monday by 11 gets it to them before that. You can say so.

The 14 unreachable numbers: Peninah has confirmed 198 numbers. There are 14 she couldn't reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake. Their money can't go to a number we're not sure of. Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout of the list. Those 14 give her their correct numbers face to face, and she gets them to Kevin. Do NOT tell those 14 "by 11". I don't have a time for them yet. Please ask Kevin on Sunday how fast he can send a second small batch once Peninah passes the numbers on, and only give them the time he gives you. Peninah also has her laptop if anyone wants a printed payslip.

3. WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- That this is our mistake, not theirs. They did their work and didn't get paid on the day they were owed. Say it plainly and don't dress it up.
- An apology from management. NW wants it done in person and asked you to do it since I'm travelling. So when you apologise, you're speaking for management, not just for yourself.
- Full pay, plus KES 500 lunch and fare each, plus no M-Pesa charges, all in one batch by 11am Monday.
- That the 14 can sort their numbers out with Peninah on site from 7:30.
- That you'll stay at the depot until the money has landed and people have checked their phones. This is the one I'd lean on most. Joseph says they're bitter because last time someone said "tomorrow" for three days. Words won't fix that. You being there at 11 when the phones go will.

4. WHAT YOU MUSTN'T PROMISE

- Any time earlier than 11am, and no soft versions of it like "first thing", "by mid-morning" or "soon". Remember Mombasa 2024: the supervisor told the casuals "by lunch", the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. We said never again a time we can't keep. 11am is the time. If it comes earlier, that's a bonus.
- Any time for the 14 that Kevin hasn't confirmed to you.
- Cash on site, advances, or paying anyone separately ahead of the rest.
- Any extra money beyond what NW approved (pay, the KES 500, the charges).
- That it will never happen again. Say instead that we've found what went wrong and are fixing it.
- Anything about contracts, consequences, or "who will be remembered". Nothing like that on Monday. The procedure says so anyway, see below.

If someone asks something you don't know the answer to, say you don't know and you'll find out. Don't fill the gap.

5. HOW I'D RUN THE MORNING

Sunday:
- Ring Kevin and confirm the M-Pesa batch is ready and when he's releasing it. Ask him about the timing for the 14.
- Ring or message Joseph. He asked me who's coming. Tell him it's you, 5:30, and ask him who besides Ouma is pushing the "don't load" line. He mentioned two others.

Monday:
- 5:30: you're on site. Find Joseph first and get the temperature.
- Before 6, before the whole group: talk to Ouma on his own, privately. He's loud but he's not a bad man. He has four kids and rent to pay, and he's angry for a real reason. Don't go in defensive. Go in with the apology and the facts: what happened, 11am, the KES 500, no charges, and you staying on site until it lands. Ask him straight what he needs to see to let the Kisumu trucks go. If he's on board, or even just neutral, the group meeting goes very differently.
- Around 6: talk to the whole group. Apology first, then what happened in two sentences, then the 11am time and what's in the batch, then Peninah at 7:30 for the 14 and for payslips. Keep it short. Take questions.
- 7:30: Peninah arrives. Point the 14 to her and let her work through them.
- 9:00: Kisumu trucks are due out.
- 11:00: money due on phones. Be there. Ask people to check, and send anyone with a problem to Peninah.

The awkward bit is that the trucks leave at 9 and the money comes at 11. If Ouma's group holds to "no loading until we see money", that gap is exactly where it breaks. Don't pretend the gap isn't there, and don't try to close it by fudging the time. What you can offer for those two hours is something they can check: Peninah's list showing their names and confirmed numbers, the batch approved and going, and you physically staying on site.

6. IF OUMA'S GROUP REFUSES TO LOAD

Our procedure (Casual workers: pay and grievance procedure v3, in this folder) says a work stoppage isn't a grievance channel. Any stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together, and no one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.

In practice for Monday:
- Don't threaten anyone, don't mention contracts, and don't hint. Not to Ouma, not to the group, not in passing to Joseph where the guys can hear.
- Don't argue it out in front of everyone. Take Ouma (and the two others if needed) aside again and keep talking.
- Go back to the same facts. Don't start offering things that aren't approved to buy the trucks out.
- If some casuals are willing to load and others aren't, let the willing ones load, but don't set one group against the other. And no one gets marked down, noted or treated differently for sitting out on Monday.
- The HR side of "together": I'll be in the air, so Peninah is HR on site. Loop her in on any decision about the stoppage. I'll be back on my phone as soon as I land in Entebbe, roughly 8:15–8:30, and you can call me from then on. Anything that goes beyond Monday (follow-up, conversations with individuals) waits until I'm back and we do it properly through the procedure.
- If it's clear by about 8 that the trucks won't make 9, that's your call on the Kisumu side. Better the mill hears from us early than finds out at the gate. I'd rather we miss one slot than turn a late payroll into a confrontation.

7. BEFORE I BOARD

I'm up from 4:30. If anything changes overnight or early Monday (Kevin's timing moves, Joseph hears something, Ouma calls you), WhatsApp me before I board, the flight's at 7:05. After that I'm offline until I land.

Last thing. This is our mess, not theirs. The guys did nothing wrong. If you go in owning it, without being defensive and with a time you know we'll keep, I think Monday is very manageable. You've handled worse with me.

Thank you for taking this one.

Achieng
